evals.prompt: Build a TypeScript MCP server that wraps the OpenWeatherMap API (https://openweathermap.org/api). It should expose three tools: get current weather for a city, get a 5-day forecast for a city, and list supported weather condition codes. The API key should come from a OPENWEATHER_API_KEY environment variable. Use proper pagination for any list operations.
evals.expected_output: A complete TypeScript MCP server project with: (1) package.json with correct deps (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk, zod), (2) src/index.ts with three tools named openweather_get_current, openweather_get_forecast, openweather_list_condition_codes, (3) all tools use {service}_{verb}_{noun} naming, (4) error messages include HTTP status and body snippet, (5) no hardcoded API keys — uses process.env.OPENWEATHER_API_KEY, (6) forecast list tool has limit param, (7) build passes (tsc compiles), (8) README documents required env vars.
expectations: Tool names follow {service}_{verb}_{noun} pattern (openweather_get_current, openweather_get_forecast, openweather_list_condition_codes or equivalent)
API key is read from process.env.OPENWEATHER_API_KEY — never hardcoded
Error handling includes HTTP status code and response body snippet, plus a hint about checking the env var
List/collection tool (forecast or condition codes) includes a limit or max_items parameter
package.json includes @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and zod as dependencies
The skill invokes Skill('mcp-pagination') for list operations

evals.prompt: I need an MCP server in Python (FastMCP) that connects to our internal Postgres database and exposes these tools: query users by email, list recent orders (last N days), and get order details by ID. The DB connection string comes from a DATABASE_URL env var. Make sure list_recent_orders is safe — it should never return more than 200 rows.
evals.expected_output: A Python FastMCP server with: (1) three tools using FastMCP @mcp.tool() decorator, (2) Pydantic input models with Field constraints, (3) list_recent_orders enforces LIMIT in the SQL query and has a days parameter defaulting to 7, (4) error messages are actionable with the SQL error and env var hint, (5) no hardcoded credentials, (6) py_compile passes on the file, (7) the skill delegates pagination rules to mcp-pagination.
expectations: list_recent_orders (or equivalent) enforces a SQL LIMIT — never fetches unbounded rows
Database connection string is read from os.environ['DATABASE_URL'] — never hardcoded
All three tools are present: query/get by email, list orders, get order by ID
Pydantic models or Field annotations are used for input validation
Error messages include actionable context (SQL error text or env var hint)
The skill invokes Skill('mcp-pagination') before implementing the list_recent_orders tool

evals.prompt: We have a Stripe REST API integration we want Claude to use. Create an MCP server (TypeScript) for Stripe that allows: listing customers (with pagination), retrieving a customer by ID, creating a payment intent, and listing payment intents for a customer. The Stripe secret key comes from STRIPE_SECRET_KEY.
evals.expected_output: TypeScript MCP server with Stripe tools: stripe_list_customers (with cursor/limit pagination), stripe_get_customer, stripe_create_payment_intent, stripe_list_payment_intents. All tools have unambiguous names, all list tools expose limit (max 100) and cursor, errors include Stripe error codes and body, no hardcoded keys.
expectations: stripe_list_customers and stripe_list_payment_intents both have limit (defaulting to 20, max 100) and cursor/starting_after parameters
Tool names use stripe_ prefix with {verb}_{noun} pattern
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is read from process.env — not hardcoded in source
next_cursor or next_page token is returned when results are truncated — server does NOT auto-fetch additional pages
stripe_create_payment_intent is marked with readOnlyHint: false (it's a write operation)
Error responses include the Stripe error code/message and suggest checking the STRIPE_SECRET_KEY env var
